summary: The UK, Canadian and German governments say their citizens need a visa for Syria, Australia says its citizens who don't have Syrian identity documents need one, and Canada says non-Arab nationals can't obtain one at border points of entry. Türkiye's foreign ministry says Turkish citizens are exempt; for Arab passports no official source we could read states the rule. Syria's embassy in Paris says entry-visa applications must be made online at evisa.sy and that it will stop receiving visa applications, and the UK and Australian governments also point to the online application. Italy's foreign ministry says that until the online platform is restored the entry visa can be requested at the border.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Syria's economy is primarily cash-based and credit cards are not widely accepted: carry enough US dollars or euros. It says ATMs in major cities such as Damascus and Aleppo are not always reliable, that because of international sanctions Canadians may not be able to use their credit and debit cards, and that exchanging currency on the street is illegal. The UK FCDO says there is minimal or no use of electronic payment systems to purchase goods.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all travel to Syria due to unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks, and says consular support is not available from the British government from within Syria. It says there is a very high threat of kidnapping from terrorists throughout Syria, and that landmines and other unexploded weapons remain, with a risk in less populated and rural areas.

tips.text: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Syria due to unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks. It says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain from the conflict and that, while highly populated areas and major routes are largely clear, a risk remains in less populated and rural areas: do not step off roads and paved areas without an experienced guide.
The UK FCDO says you may be refused entry if your passport shows previous travel to Israel, and that holders of Israeli citizenship cannot enter Syria.

Canada says credit cards are not widely accepted and to carry enough US dollars or euros, that ATMs are not always reliable, and that because of international sanctions Canadians may not be able to use their credit and debit cards. It says exchanging currency on the street is illegal: exchange money only in banks or at official exchange counters.

Canada says roadblocks and checkpoints are common, including on major roads and highways in and around major cities and along the highways connecting Damascus to Aleppo, Jordan and Beirut. The UK FCDO says you must carry copies of your passport photo page and visa for identification, and Canada says it is prohibited to photograph official buildings such as military or government installations.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Syria?
faq.answer: The UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all say their citizens need a visa, and Canada says non-Arab nationals can't obtain one at border points of entry. Türkiye's foreign ministry says Turkish citizens are exempt. For Arab passports no official source we could read states the rule. Syria's embassy in Paris says entry-visa applications must be made online at evisa.sy and that it will stop receiving visa applications; the UK and Australian governments also point to the online application. Italy's foreign ministry says that until the online platform is restored the entry visa can be requested at the border.

faq.question: Can I get a Syrian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Canada says non-Arab nationals can't obtain a visa at border points of entry and must obtain it from the nearest Syrian embassy or consulate before departure. Germany's Federal Foreign Office says Syrian visas cannot always be issued at Syria's border crossings with neighbouring countries. Italy's foreign ministry says that until the online platform is restored the visa can be requested at the border, at the land crossings from Jordan and Lebanon and at Damascus and Aleppo airports.

faq.question: Is Syria safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Syria due to unpredictable security conditions and the threat of terrorist attacks, and says terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks. It says landmines and other unexploded weapons remain, with a risk in less populated and rural areas, and that journalists and other foreign nationals may be at increased risk of detention, mistreatment or harassment by armed groups and security forces.

faq.question: What money should I use in Syria?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the economy is primarily cash-based, credit cards are not widely accepted and you should carry enough US dollars or euros to cover your expenses; ATMs in major cities such as Damascus and Aleppo are not always reliable. It says exchanging currency on the street is illegal: you must exchange foreign currency in banks or at official exchange counters.

faq.question: Can I visit Syria if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: The UK government says holders of Israeli citizenship cannot enter Syria, and that if your passport shows previous travel to Israel you may be refused entry.
